desc: The shared vocabularies: reference kinds, events, vote thresholds, motion classes, temporal anchors. One namespace: references are kind/id (e.g. motion/amend, guard/no-question-pending, state/tabled, event/stated, queue/general-orders-current, class/bylaws, order/<id>, timer/table-expiry, table/appeal-yield-matrix). Kinds are closed naming law.

reference_kinds.table: named decision tables (precedence.json, voting.json, rules.json, scheduler.json)
reference_kinds.order: rules.json order objects (adopted debate-limiting orders etc.)
reference_kinds.question: lifecycle question object instances (runtime)

events.desc: One event vocabulary. 'origin' names the part that emits it. Core events are usable everywhere; prefer reuse over coining.

core.desc: a vote is being retaken by another (or a counted) method — division, retake-by-other-method motion, or chair's own retake

protocol_additional.desc: the chair announces a ruling; opens the appeal window
the chair failed to respond to a duly made point of order, appeal, or motion; recorded per occurrence — the counter behind the member self-put remedy
the chair, without objection, permits a brief pause without declaring a recess; no interruption of the meeting
the chair declares the meeting again in order, or any member objects to continuing to stand at ease
an absent electee without prior consent is notified; the election becomes final unless they immediately decline
a timer instance crossed its expires_at boundary; time as an event source — fires recomputation of available_actions (INTERFACE execution model)
a breach of order observed at its moment; the point-of-order timeliness anchor
debate or business has intervened since the last announcement; closes challenge windows
an adopted motion's declared purpose creates a connected series of motions toward one object
the chair directs the secretary to read a paper
nominations closed (by motion, two-thirds, or by the chair when no further nominations are offered)

scheduler_additional.desc: the assembly voted against proceeding to the orders of the day
the announced or moved item departs from the dispatch order (agenda, program, or order of business being varied from; or a postponed motion's time arrived or passed unannounced)

engine_additional.desc: the making of a reconsider is in progress (outranks everything at making time)

lifecycle.desc: a reconsider of this question's vote was made and seconded but not taken up; the hold begins
the hold ended without the reconsider being adopted: rejected, withdrawn, call-up window expired, or fallen to ground at session end
committee reports the referred question back
a postponed question's set time reached (via scheduler)
unfinished business reached in the order of business

thresholds.desc: Canonical vote-threshold vocabulary. A motion's vote field lists sufficient alternatives — any one suffices. Compound forms combine previous notice with a threshold.

values.desc: more than half of votes cast
at least two thirds of votes cast
sustained by two thirds voting in the negative (e.g. objection-to-consideration: 'shall the question be considered')
chair's ruling stands unless a majority votes in the negative (appeal)
majority of all registered voting members (convention contexts)

majority of the members present — possible but generally undesirable (abstention acts as a negative); the negative is not taken (intrinsically irrelevant) and the chair counts those present immediately after the affirmative, before attendance can change
two thirds of the members present; same mechanics and caveats as majority-present
effective on the demand of one member; no vote taken
decided by the chair's ruling, not a vote (appealable where applicable)
no question is put at all; the chair responds or acts (inquiries, requests answered directly)

motion_classes.B: bring-back (motions that bring a question again before the assembly)
motion_classes.M/B: main motion of the bring-back kind

temporal_anchors.desc: Timers reference these named anchors, never raw durations.
